text:
emma: Draft PRD for authz: scoped tokens + org/project RBAC posted — https://docs.redwood.example/prd/authz-scoped-tokens. TL;DR: support API keys, org roles, and project-scoped tokens usable for CI/deploys. Asking: agree on v1 scope, acceptance criteria, and risky edge cases?

sai: skimmed it. good baseline. question: are scoped tokens revocable per-project or per-org only?

emma: goal v1: per-token revocation and per-project scoping. revocation flows: token id -> invalidate cache -> persist blacklisted id. open to tradeoffs if too slow.

oliver: I'd push back on blacklists for scale. prefer versioned signing keys + 'iat' and short TTL for tokens. revocation would be rotate sign key + warn older tokens expire.

marina: tradeoff summary: blacklist -> immediate revoke but stateful; key rotation -> stateless but delayed revoke. we should pick one for v1.

jordan: for customer asks (enterprise) they want immediate revoke from console. so v1 must support explicit revoke for tokens created via Console + API.

sai: OK, then we need hybrid: short TTL (1h) + ability to mark token id revoked for console/API revokes. blacklist limited to active tokens in last 24h to bound size.

emma: proposed acceptance criteria (v1):
- API: create/list/revoke tokens. tokens have optional `project_id` claim.
- RBAC: 3 built-in roles at org-level: owner/admin/member; project-level role mapping can restrict actions.
- Console: UI to create project-scoped token and revoke it. audit log entry for create/revoke.
- Security: tokens are 32-byte random secrets, stored hashed, rotated signing keys, and short TTL for JS SDK usage.
- Tests: e2e that verifies project-scoped token cannot access other-project resources.

oliver: add acceptance: gateway enforces token->project claim and rejects cross-project header like `X-Project-ID` mismatch. Also integration test for cache invalidation latency < 5s after revoke.

marina: edge cases:
- what happens on org transfer (user moves project to another org)? tokens must become invalid.
- existing API keys migration: we currently have global API keys with no project claims. migration path?
- service accounts: tokens created by service principals vs user tokens (different rotation/lifespan).

emma: migration options in PRD:
1) soft compatibility: accept legacy keys but they are treated as org-scoped (no project claim) and flagged in Console to encourage rotate.
2) migration tool: map legacy key -> new project-scoped token when user selects project.
Decision: ship option 1 in v1, tool in v2.

sai: downstream implications for rate limits and quotas — project-scoped tokens should be billed to project. need billing tags in logs. add to acceptance.

jordan: also need clear launch criteria for enterprise: SLA for revoke (console) and audit retention 90d. if we can't meet 90d at GA, add as premium feature.

emma: proposed launch checklist (v1):
- API endpoints + validation (create/list/revoke, list by project)
- Console flows + audit log entry UI
- Policy enforcement in runtime (reject cross-project access)
- Hybrid revoke system implemented + tests for <5s invalidate
- Docs + migration guidance + changelog
- E2E tests + load tests (blacklist size bounded)

oliver: note on runtime: we'll integrate with existing auth middleware. minimal perf hit if blacklist hit-rate is low. add metrics: blacklist_hits, revoke_latency.

marina: security review items: KMS for signing keys, HSM integration flag for enterprise, and ensure logs don't contain token plaintext.

access-bot: deploy-preview: authz/scoped-tokens branch built (staging). smoke tests: create/revoke token OK, cross-project blocked.

sai: thanks. next: I'll update RFC with hybrid revoke details and TTL defaults (1h token, refresh tokens for long lived sessions) and add test plans.

emma: can folks comment on the PRD doc by EOD? specifically: acceptance criteria, migration plan, and console UX text. @oliver @marina @jordan

oliver: will do, small comments incoming. :thumbsup:

marina: will add security checklist and SSO notes (defer SSO integration to v2).

emma: great — plan to cut an RFC on Monday and spin up implementation tickets. thanks all.
